title: Biosphere Reserves in India and the MAB Programme

cards.b:
Biosphere reserves are a Prelims favourite because the statements mix them with national parks and sanctuaries. The big difference: biosphere reserves are not created by the Wildlife (Protection) Act. They are a UNESCO idea carried out through the central government.

Learn the zones, the list and the first one.

UNESCO launched the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme in 1971. The World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR) began in 1976. Sites stay under national law and are nominated by countries.

An Indian biosphere reserve is declared by the central government on the scheme Biosphere Reserve Programme, run by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). It tries to join conservation with use by local people.

Each reserve is arranged in three zones.

  • Core: legally protected, minimal human activity, undisturbed.
  • Buffer: surrounds the core; research, education and limited use allowed.
  • Transition: outer area where people live and farm, working with managers.

Three functions: conservation, development (sustainable) and logistic support (research and monitoring).

India's first biosphere reserve was the Nilgiri (1986), spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. India has 18 biosphere reserves designated by the government. Examples:

  • Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand), Khangchendzonga (Sikkim), Nokrek (Meghalaya)
  • Sundarbans (West Bengal), Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu)
  • Great Nicobar, Simlipal (Odisha), Pachmarhi (Madhya Pradesh)
  • Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Agasthyamala, Panna, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dihang-Dibang

The UNESCO network includes about twelve of these (as of 2020; check the latest).

• Gulf of Mannar was the first marine biosphere reserve in South Asia.
  • Sundarbans is a mangrove and tiger landscape, also a Ramsar site and World Heritage Site.
  • Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers are a World Heritage Site together.
  • Panna (2020) was among the recent UNESCO additions.

Check whether a name asked in an exam is in the UNESCO list or only the Indian list.

A national park has fixed legal boundaries and bans grazing and private rights. A biosphere reserve is larger, has zones, and may include national parks and sanctuaries inside. A conservation reserve and community reserve are WPA categories on government and community land.

So a biosphere reserve is a planning layer. The legal teeth come from the park or sanctuary inside it.

Critics say biosphere reserves lack a dedicated law, so rules in buffer and transition zones are weak. Local people may not gain from them. Funding is thin, and boundaries are often drawn without community consent.

Supporters argue they are the only model that accepts people living in a landscape, which fits India.

Many Indian reserves are home to forest communities. Tribal groups in Nilgiri (Todas, Kotas) and Nokrek (Garo) depend on resources there. The Forest Rights Act 2006 and joint forest management link to biosphere zones. In Sundarbans, mangrove fishing and honey collection need regulated use.

The Nilgiri reserve also protects the Silent Valley and Mukurthi areas, and holds the Nilgiri tahr and the lion-tailed macaque.

• MAB launched: 1971.
  • First Indian reserve: Nilgiri, 1986.
  • Zones: core, buffer, transition.
  • Not created by the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
  • Nodal ministry: MoEFCC.

Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Gulf of Mannar and Nilgiri are the most asked names. A good habit is to link each reserve with its state and its flagship species before the exam.

Prelims-style: "Which of the following are biosphere reserves?" Check Nokrek, Simlipal, Pachmarhi. Remember that Kanha is a tiger reserve and national park, not a biosphere reserve.

Mains-style: "How are biosphere reserves different from national parks? Do they help both conservation and people?" Structure: definition; zones; difference; examples; limits; reform.

quiz.q: The MAB Programme was launched by:
Which zone of a biosphere reserve is legally protected and undisturbed?
quiz.w: Core is the most protected zone.

quiz.q: Biosphere reserves in India are not created under:
Gulf of Mannar is best known as:
How many biosphere reserves has India designated?
quiz.w: As of recent years; UNESCO recognises about twelve.

quiz.q: Which is a biosphere reserve in Meghalaya?
quiz.w: Nokrek is the Garo Hills reserve.

quiz.q: Which Ministry runs the Biosphere Reserve Programme?

quiz.w: It protects the core from outside pressures.
